name: Question 12
problem:
Consider the curve defined parametrically as 

$$
x={e}^{t}-t,\,y=4{e}^{t/2},\,t\in [0,1].
$$

Calculate the surface area generated when this curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi x\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${t}_{1}=0$ to ${t}_{2}=1.$ 

Computing the derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}-t)={e}^{t}-1 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{e}^{t/2})=2{e}^{t/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{t}-t)\sqrt{{({e}^{t}-1)}^{2}+{(2{e}^{t/2})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{t}-t)\sqrt{{e}^{2t}-2{e}^{t}+1+4{e}^{t}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{t}-t)\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+2{e}^{t}+1}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, factoring the expression ${e}^{2t}+2{e}^{t}+1,$ we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{t}-t)\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+2{e}^{t}+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{t}-t)\sqrt{({e}^{t}+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{t}-t)\cdot |{e}^{t}+1|\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{t}-t)\cdot ({e}^{t}+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{2t}+{e}^{t}-t{e}^{t}-t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi [{\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{2t}+{e}^{t}-t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{0}^{1}t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t]\end{aligned}
$$

We evaluate the integral ${\int }_{0}^{1}t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t$ using integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{t} & ⇒ & v={e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}x & =t{e}^{t}-\int {e}^{t}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =t{e}^{t}-{e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi [{\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{2t}+{e}^{t}-t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{0}^{1}t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t] \\  & =2\pi [{(\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}+{e}^{t}-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2})|}_{0}^{1}-{(t{e}^{t}-{e}^{t})|}_{0}^{1}] \\  & =2\pi [(\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}+e-\frac{1}{2})-(\frac{1}{2}+1-0)-(e-e)+(0-1)] \\  & =2\pi [\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}+e-3] \\  & =({e}^{2}+2e-6)\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

html:
Question 12
?

Consider the curve defined parametrically as x=et−t,y=4et/2,t∈[0,1]. Calculate the surface area generated when this curve is rotated 2π radians about the y-axis.

a
 (2e2−e+3)π
b
 (e2+6e)π
c
 (e2+3e−1)π
d
 (e2−3)π
e
 (e2+2e−6)π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated 2π radians about the y-axis using the formula

S=∫2πxds.

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

ds=(dxdt)2+(dydt)2dt. Therefore, we will use

S=2π∫t1t2x(dxdt)2+(dydt)2dt.

We are told that the limits of integration are from t1=0 to t2=1.

Computing the derivatives, we get

dxdt=ddt(et−t)=et−1dydt=ddt(4et/2)=2et/2.

Therefore,

S=2π∫t1t2x(dxdt)2+(dydt)2dt=2π∫01(et−t)(et−1)2+(2et/2)2dt=2π∫01(et−t)e2t−2et+1+4etdt=2π∫01(et−t)e2t+2et+1dt

Now, factoring the expression e2t+2et+1, we can rewrite our integral as follows:

S=2π∫01(et−t)e2t+2et+1dt=2π∫01(et−t)(et+1)2dt=2π∫01(et−t)⋅|et+1|dt=2π∫01(et−t)⋅(et+1)dt=2π∫01(e2t+et−tet−t)dt=2π[∫01(e2t+et−t)dt−∫01tetdt]

We evaluate the integral ∫01tetdt using integration by parts. We set u=t⇒u′=1v′=et⇒v=et.

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get ∫tetdx=tet−∫et⋅1dx=tet−et.

Therefore, we get

S=2π[∫01(e2t+et−t)dt−∫01tetdt]=2π[(12e2t+et−12t2)|01−(tet−et)|01]=2π[(12e2+e−12)−(12+1−0)−(e−e)+(0−1)]=2π[12e2+e−3]=(e2+2e−6)π.
